biography: Paul Keller, a name whispered with a mix of excitement and frustration in the Swiss racing paddocks, hails from the small village of Interlaken. His journey began not on asphalt, but on snow, mastering the art of control while navigating treacherous mountain roads in his grandfather's vintage rally car. It was during one particularly daring winter drive, narrowly avoiding a collision with a runaway sled, that the elder Keller recognized a raw talent in his grandson – a preternatural ability to react and a fearless dedication to speed. Paul transitioned to karting at 15, quickly dominating the local scene. A defining moment came at the Swiss National Karting Championship, where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he carved his way through the field to win in the final corner. This victory caught the attention of a Porsche junior team, leading to his current position driving the iconic Porsche 911 RSR 74. Now at 22, in what many consider his peak physical condition, Paul remains an enigma. His raw speed is undeniable, but his inconsistency often leaves team strategists tearing their hair out. He is currently aiming for a podium finish in the upcoming European Endurance Championship.
drivingStyle: Keller's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from the car, often pushing the limits of grip to an almost reckless degree. He attacks corners with an aggressive late-braking technique, relying on his exceptional reflexes to maintain control. While his tire management can be erratic, on his day, he can deliver blistering lap times that leave competitors in awe. He tends to thrive under pressure, often producing his best results when the stakes are highest, but he is also prone to making costly mistakes when he feels unchallenged.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A veteran driver known for his tactical prowess, Dubois represents everything Keller isn't: calculated, consistent, and patient. Dubois publicly criticized Keller's aggressive driving style, sparking a heated rivalry both on and off the track.

rivalries.name: Isabella Rossi
rivalries.reason: Rossi, a rising star from Italy, shares Keller's penchant for daring overtakes. Their battles on track are legendary, often resulting in close calls and accusations of dangerous driving. There's a grudging respect between them, but neither is willing to yield an inch.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka, a stoic Japanese driver, is Keller's teammate. While there is no outward animosity, a quiet rivalry simmers beneath the surface as they constantly compete to be the team's lead driver, fueling tension within the Porsche camp.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, which are threadbare and smell faintly of Swiss cheese, for every race.
Insists on listening to a specific obscure yodeling song before getting into the car.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
nickname: The Interlaken Iceman (when he's calm), The Swiss Tornado (when he's not)
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being perfect; it's about being faster than perfect."
careerHighlight: Winning the rain-soaked Spa-Francorchamps 24 Hours in 2023. Against all odds, Keller executed a series of daring overtakes in the final hour, securing victory for his team and cementing his reputation as a fearless driver.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2024 Le Mans 24 Hours with only two hours remaining. A mechanical failure sent him spinning into the barriers, costing his team a likely victory and leaving Keller devastated.
